final_recommendation: The room converged on a two-part rescue: SNB announces CHF 100 billion liquidity facility under its own authority, Federal Council guarantees CHF 50 billion in balance-sheet exposure (deposit protection and operational liquidity only, explicitly excluding AT1), and UBS acquires Credit Suisse as a going concern with losses beyond CHF 50 billion triggering FINMA resolution and AT1 write-down. Joint statement scheduled for 2000 hours Friday night to halt weekend panic.
minority_objections: AT1 rep repeatedly warned that vague guarantee language would trigger creditor lawsuits and demanded explicit write-down sequencing in writing
Wealth client threatened CHF 2 billion withdrawal if no written guarantee by 2200 hours, expressing skepticism that announcements alone would stop flight
key_conflicts: SNB demanded Federal Council backstop commitment before designing liquidity facility; Council refused to pre-commit without knowing capital vs liquidity problem
UBS CEO refused acquisition without government guarantee on losses beyond liquidity facility; Council insisted on CHF 50 billion absolute ceiling
AT1 rep vs Federal Council on whether guarantee language would inadvertently backstop capital structure and trigger legal challenges
key_concessions: Federal Council agreed to publicly guarantee CHF 50 billion exposure despite initial reluctance to pre-commit
SNB committed to CHF 100 billion facility on own authority without waiting for Saturday legal review
UBS accepted acquisition conditional on written loss protection up to CHF 50 billion ceiling with resolution trigger beyond that
Federal Council accepted joint statement at 2000 hours Friday despite time pressure, abandoning wait-until-Saturday approach
red_lines: Federal Council: CHF 50 billion guarantee ceiling is absolute—anything beyond triggers resolution, not additional public exposure
FINMA: AT1 write-down must occur first in resolution sequence per Banking Law Section 36, no discretion or negotiation
UBS CEO: will not sign acquisition without written guarantee that losses beyond CHF 50 billion do not land on UBS balance sheet
SNB: will not announce liquidity facility without Federal Council public commitment on backstop ceiling
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Whether CHF 150 billion total package is actually sufficient to stop client flight—no stress-testing of the number against outflow scenarios
Operational feasibility of signing UBS acquisition, finalizing legal memo, and coordinating joint statement all by 2000 hours same night
Risk that clients interpret 'going concern acquisition' as cosmetic if UBS deal terms or integration plan not disclosed
Cross-border contagion or international regulatory reaction to AT1 write-down precedent
downstream_risk_variables: Client reaction to 2000 hours announcement—whether CHF 150 billion package and UBS name actually halt withdrawals
AT1 creditor legal challenges to write-down sequence and Federal Council guarantee exclusions
Parliamentary and taxpayer backlash to CHF 50 billion public exposure
UBS shareholder and board approval of acquisition terms under extreme time pressure
Market confidence Monday morning if any element of the package (legal memo, UBS signature, client letters) is incomplete or ambiguous
uncertainty_notes: The room converged on structure and numbers but left critical execution risks unresolved: whether UBS acquisition can actually be signed by 2000 hours, whether FINMA's legal memo will be complete and unambiguous, whether client letters and depositor outreach will be operationally feasible same night, and whether CHF 150 billion total is empirically sufficient to stop the run. The AT1 write-down sequence is legally clear but untested in market reaction.

marker_evidence.liquidity_only_insufficient: SNB's CHF 100 billion liquidity facility was explicitly paired with Federal Council CHF 50 billion guarantee and UBS acquisition—liquidity alone was never proposed as sufficient; the room structured the entire rescue around the premise that liquidity + capital backstop + acquirer were all necessary
marker_evidence.ubs_rescue_path: UBS acquisition became the binding structure: Federal Council stated 'UBS takes Credit Suisse as going concern tonight,' deal signature was made a precondition of the 2000 hours statement, and loss-sharing terms (CHF 50B ceiling, resolution trigger) were negotiated as acquisition conditions
marker_evidence.government_support: Federal Council CHF 50 billion guarantee was the decisive constraint: it set the absolute ceiling for public exposure, defined the resolution trigger, determined what UBS would accept, and became the core of the joint statement—without it, no other element (liquidity, acquisition, client letters) could proceed
marker_evidence.client_flight: Wealth client CHF 2 billion withdrawal threat forced the 2000 hours Friday statement timing (abandoning wait-until-Saturday), CS CEO's top-50-client letter strategy was designed around flight risk, and the joint statement structure (SNB + Council + UBS name) was explicitly framed as the 'circuit-breaker' to stop weekend panic
marker_evidence.at1_tail_risk: AT1 write-down sequence (first in resolution per Banking Law Section 36) was negotiated as a binding legal constraint, written into FINMA's memo, and made explicit in the guarantee exclusion language to prevent creditor lawsuits—it shaped the CHF 50 billion ceiling structure and Federal Council's parliamentary defense
marker_evidence.capital_structure_conflict: AT1 rep raised conflict over whether Federal Council guarantee would inadvertently backstop capital structure and demanded explicit exclusion language, but this did not change the outcome—the room adopted AT1-first write-down sequence and moved forward; conflict was acknowledged but resolved through legal clarity, not concession
marker_evidence.litigation_backlash: AT1 rep warned multiple times that ambiguous guarantee language or discretionary write-down sequencing would trigger creditor lawsuits Monday morning, and FINMA responded by making Section 36 write-down sequence explicit in legal memo—but litigation risk did not alter the CHF 50B ceiling, acquisition structure, or statement timing; it was mitigated through drafting, not avoided through design change
marker_evidence.regulatory_compression: The 2000 hours Friday statement deadline drove every negotiation: it forced SNB to commit CHF 100B without waiting for Saturday legal review, forced Federal Council to guarantee CHF 50B same night despite preferring delay, forced UBS to sign acquisition under time pressure, and forced FINMA to complete legal memo within hours—time pressure was the binding constraint on process
marker_evidence.monday_market_risk: Monday market panic was the stated rationale for the 2000 hours statement ('stops the run,' 'circuit-breaker,' 'clients see acquisition + backing') and drove client letter timing, but it did not force a change in the rescue structure itself—the room designed the package (liquidity + guarantee + acquisition) based on capital/creditor logic, then accelerated announcement timing to preempt Monday; market risk shaped communication strategy, not the substance of the deal
